description: Source-of-truth mapping of 'when code changes, which docs must be updated in the same commit/PR'. Consumed by tools/docs-sync/check_docs_sync.py and AGENTS.md.

rules.title: AssembleKit framework changes must update architecture.md
rules.rationale: Public Page / ViewPage / Assembly / ListPage / scoped locals API and behaviour are documented in architecture.md (§ AssembleKit, § AssembleKit v2). Any source change in this folder MUST be reflected there.

rules.title: Dependency-rule task changes must update module-rules.md
rules.rationale: CheckDependencyRulesTask.kt is the single source of truth for layer enforcement. Its docs lives in module-rules.md.

rules.title: Gradle module include changes must update structure docs
rules.rationale: settings.gradle.kts changes typically add/remove a module. Architecture diagram, module-rules examples, and README structure all need to stay in sync.

rules.title: Router path table changes must update architecture.md
rules.rationale: Router.Paths is the cross-feature navigation contract; the path table is described in architecture.md.

rules.title: CI workflow changes must update architecture.md or README
rules.rationale: When CI jobs are added/removed/reordered, the 'CI' section in architecture.md and the readme overview must reflect it.

rules.title: New tooling scripts must be documented
rules.rationale: Every Python/shell tool under tools/ is part of the engineering surface; it needs an entry in architecture.md or its own README so newcomers can find it.

rules.title: New / renamed Convention Plugins must update architecture.md
rules.rationale: Convention Plugin IDs (demo.android.application / .feature / .foundation / .bizlib …) are referenced verbatim in architecture.md.

rules.title: New libraries / version-catalog additions must update architecture.md
rules.rationale: Adding a new library (e.g. recyclerview, mavericks, future compose) is a stack-level decision and must be reflected in the architecture stack overview.

notes: Rules are evaluated against the union of: committed changes between base...HEAD, staged changes, and unstaged changes. CI uses base = origin/main.
A rule fails when its triggers match changed files but none of its required docs are also in the changed set.
Use skip_markers in any commit message in the PR to bypass a rule when it genuinely does not apply (e.g. pure refactor with no behaviour change). Justify the skip in the PR description.
